Job Description

The Iowa Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Water Quality Bureau is seeking a dynamic, self-starting, and highly collaborative professional to fill the role of Water Quality GIS Analyst (Geologist 3). This position is tailored for an energetic team player who enjoys working in a cross-functional environment and possesses the drive to take complex technical initiatives and independently run with them. Rather than operating in a data silo, you will serve as a vital storyteller and relationship-builder, bridging the gap between advanced spatial analytics and human-centric teamwork. You will work closely with a diverse team of internal water quality professionals, stakeholders, and state and federal agency partners to support the implementation of the Clean Water Act By turning complex monitoring data into clear, interactive visual tools, you will directly enhance public resource management with critical water quality spatial data.

Advanced Spatial Modeling & Clean Water Act Data Analysis

At the core of this role is the independent execution of high-level spatial analyses and data visualization using ESRI's ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and Spatial Analyst tools. The daily workflow involves processing LiDAR elevation data, applying basic remote sensing principles, and performing spatial modeling to simulate critical environmental processes such as erosion, sedimentation, nutrient transport, and runoff. You will be responsible for creating interactive online resources, paper and electronic maps, and digital story maps that translate Water Quality Monitoring and Assessment (WQMA) data into meaningful tools for public education and decision-making. Additional core responsibilities include managing data across various WQMA databases, maintaining detailed metadata, and collaborating with program staff to identify lake or wetland footprints and map impaired waters coverages for the biennial 303(d)/305(b) Integrated Report.

Watershed Project Development & Field Implementation

This position demands a proactive approach to watershed project development, field implementation, and post-project evaluation. You will provide essential GIS data and technical guidance to watershed sponsors and project coordinators, utilizing tools like the Agricultural Conservation Planning Framework (ACPF) and custom watershed characterization models. Furthermore, you will design mobile tools to collect field data and facilitate watershed fieldwork assessments targeting tillage practices, streambank and shoreline erosion, stream corridor characterization, and the location and condition of existing Best Management Practices (BMPs).

GIS Training, Technical Mentorship, & Liaison Duties

A defining aspect of this role is serving as an active technical mentor and educator for the bureau. You will regularly provide one-on-one coaching and organized training sessions to assist non-GIS professional staff and local project partners with basic to intermediate GIS needs and nonpoint source pollution reduction calculations. To build long-term capacity, you will author clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and build user-friendly map templates so that fellow staff can generate their own ongoing GIS products. Your communication and presentation skills will be utilized as you represent the Department at regional or national meetings, deliver formal presentations to public stakeholders, and serve as a liaison with other state and federal agencies. Finally, you will support data governance by collaborating with DNR staff and the Department of Management Division of Information Technology (DOM-DoIT) to establish unified enterprise data standards for all GIS-related projects.

Develops and maintains effective working relationships with staff, other state and federal agencies, , the regulated public, industry professionals, and local stakeholders
Works closely with Water Quality Bureau Program staff to analyze data sets in order to effectively display and communicate water quality data. Create SOPs and templates so other bureau staff can produce their own ongoing GIS products for their projects.
Work with water quality bureau staff on projects relating to the implementation of the Clean Water Act by utilizing GIS software and other computer software products.

The Iowa Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Water Quality Bureau is seeking a dynamic, self-starting, and highly collaborative professional to fill the role of Water Quality GIS Analyst (Geologist 3). This position is tailored for an energetic team player who enjoys working in a cross-functional environment and possesses the drive to take complex technical initiatives and independently run with them. Rather than operating in a data silo, you will serve as a vital storyteller and relationship-builder, bridging the gap between advanced spatial analytics and human-centric teamwork. You will work closely with a diverse team of internal water quality professionals, stakeholders, and state and federal agency partners to support the implementation of the Clean Water Act By turning complex monitoring data into clear, interactive visual tools, you will directly enhance public resource management with critical water quality spatial data.

Advanced Spatial Modeling & Clean Water Act Data Analysis

At the core of this role is the independent execution of high-level spatial analyses and data visualization using ESRI's ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and Spatial Analyst tools. The daily workflow involves processing LiDAR elevation data, applying basic remote sensing principles, and performing spatial modeling to simulate critical environmental processes such as erosion, sedimentation, nutrient transport, and runoff. You will be responsible for creating interactive online resources, paper and electronic maps, and digital story maps that translate Water Quality Monitoring and Assessment (WQMA) data into meaningful tools for public education and decision-making. Additional core responsibilities include managing data across various WQMA databases, maintaining detailed metadata, and collaborating with program staff to identify lake or wetland footprints and map impaired waters coverages for the biennial 303(d)/305(b) Integrated Report.

Watershed Project Development & Field Implementation

This position demands a proactive approach to watershed project development, field implementation, and post-project evaluation. You will provide essential GIS data and technical guidance to watershed sponsors and project coordinators, utilizing tools like the Agricultural Conservation Planning Framework (ACPF) and custom watershed characterization models. Furthermore, you will design mobile tools to collect field data and facilitate watershed fieldwork assessments targeting tillage practices, streambank and shoreline erosion, stream corridor characterization, and the location and condition of existing Best Management Practices (BMPs).

GIS Training, Technical Mentorship, & Liaison Duties

A defining aspect of this role is serving as an active technical mentor and educator for the bureau. You will regularly provide one-on-one coaching and organized training sessions to assist non-GIS professional staff and local project partners with basic to intermediate GIS needs and nonpoint source pollution reduction calculations. To build long-term capacity, you will author clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and build user-friendly map templates so that fellow staff can generate their own ongoing GIS products. Your communication and presentation skills will be utilized as you represent the Department at regional or national meetings, deliver formal presentations to public stakeholders, and serve as a liaison with other state and federal agencies. Job Summary
The Extension Program Coordinator will support and assist in the management of the Master Gardener Volunteer programs and other Horticulture Extension related programs for adults and youth. Duties & Responsibilities

Program Coordination and Development
Coordinate the planning of educational activities for the program with collaboration from the County Director or Educator.
Identifies critical priority needs and issues, with the assistance of other staff, to be addressed through Master Gardener programs.
Conduct evaluation of program activities and make appropriate changes or recommendation for continuation or discontinuation of the program.
Provide leadership, as primary contact, to volunteers, Master Gardeners in support of local Master Gardener programs and their activities.
Provide leadership for the local Expansion and Review Committee.
Work with Unit staff, Extension volunteers, and Extension clientele to create and/or maintain administrative records.
Disseminate education information provided by Extension professionals.
Maintain required records and data.
Provides monthly reports to the County Extension Director.

Skills in communicating and collaborating with all audiences

Ability to operate computer systems.
Attention to detail and prioritize tasks. Ability to multi-task.

Job Description

The Iowa Judicial Branch is seeking applicants for a Program Coordinator within Children’s Justice for Family Treatment Court in Cass County and other Children’s Justice programs within District 4. The domicile for the position will be located within District 4 which includes Harrison, Shelby, Audubon, Pottawattamie, Cass, Mills, Montgomery, Fremont and Page counties and will be decided by the supervisor.

This position will coordinate the day-to-day operations of the Family Treatment Court or like programs in Judicial District 4 as well as support the implementation of a Family Resiliency Center in Council Bluffs. This position will manage referrals, intake, and orientation with families, and serve as the first line of communication between families and the court team. This position will collect and maintain accurate case data, serve as a liaison between families, treatment teams, and community service providers, and support program improvement through data analysis and compliance reporting. This position may occasionally attend court hearings, community events, and coordinator meetings both in person and virtually, with availability for evening meetings as needed.

The successful candidate will be able to learn and navigate case management systems and program-specific technology to maintain current and accurate records and materials. This position will have the ability to professionally communicate and build relationships with a variety of individuals including parents, judges, treatment team members, and community partners. The successful candidate will have a trauma-informed, strengths-based approach to family engagement and keen attention to detail to ensure the accuracy and integrity of case data and compliance reporting. This position will also coordinate training opportunities and multi-disciplinary team functions to support the ongoing development of the Family Treatment Court model. This position will involve travel to other counties within the judicial district as well as occasional travel outside of District 4.
